summary: Specifies the code point used for OSPFv3 in the Segment ID sub-TLV and the Downstream Detailed Mapping TLV of MPLS LSP Ping. RFC 8287 had defined code points for OSPF and IS-IS. This document updates RFC 8287 by clarifying how they apply.

eli5.summary: A list of codes for network testing tools was missing one entry, and this adds it.

questions: ospfv3 code point for mpls lsp ping
mpls lsp ping segment id sub-tlv
what is the ospfv3 code point for mpls lsp ping
what protocol value is ospfv3 in the segment id sub-tlv
subtitle: Gives OSPFv3 its own protocol value in MPLS LSP Ping and pins the old OSPF value to OSPFv2.

tldr.problem: RFC 8287 defined protocol code points for OSPF and IS-IS in MPLS LSP Ping, but had none for OSPFv3, which carries IPv6 and can also advertise IPv4 prefixes.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9214 assigns value 3 (OSPFv3) in the Segment ID sub-TLV protocol registry and value 7 in the Downstream Detailed Mapping registry, and says the existing OSPF values are for OSPFv2 only.
tldr.outcome: A responder can now validate a segment against the right OSPF version. The document updates RFC 8287.

today: RFC 9214 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 8287; no later RFC is recorded as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
MPLS LSP Ping checks whether a label switched path works. RFC 8287 extended it for Segment Routing and defined protocol code points for OSPF and IS-IS. IANA keeps two registries for them under the MPLS LSP Ping Parameters registry: "Protocol in the Segment ID Sub-TLV" and "Protocol in Label Stack Sub-TLV of Downstream Detailed Mapping TLV".

RFC 5340 describes OSPF version 3 (OSPFv3) for IPv6, and RFC 5838 lets it carry several address families, so OSPFv3 may advertise both IPv6 and IPv4 prefixes. RFC 9214 fills the gap: it names the code point to use when the IGP is OSPFv3.
sections.eli5: Testing tools label each message with the kind of routing system behind it. There was a label for the old kind, but not for the newer one that handles the newer kind of address.

sections.title: What the Reader Is Expected to Know
sections.content: The document builds on the terminology of RFC 8402 (Segment Routing Architecture), RFC 8029 (detecting MPLS data-plane failures) and RFC 8287 (LSP Ping and Traceroute for Segment Routing). Readers are expected to be familiar with all three. It uses the RFC 2119 and RFC 8174 key words, such as MUST and SHOULD, only when written in capitals.
sections.eli5: This note is a small add-on to bigger manuals, so you are supposed to have read those first.

sections.title: OSPFv3 in Segment ID Sub-TLVs
sections.content:
When the protocol field of a Segment ID sub-TLV of Type 34 (IPv4 IGP-Prefix Segment ID), Type 35 (IPv6 IGP-Prefix Segment ID) or Type 36 (IGP-Adjacency Segment ID) is set to 3, the responder MUST do Forwarding Equivalence Class (FEC) validation using OSPFv3 as the IGP.

The initiator MUST NOT set the protocol field of Type 35 and Type 36 sub-TLVs to OSPF (value 1), because OSPFv2 is not compatible with the IPv6 addresses those sub-TLVs indicate.

To cope with older implementations that used value 1 to mean OSPFv3, a responder that receives value 1 in a Type 35 or Type 36 sub-TLV MAY treat it as "Any IGP Protocol" (value 0), following step 4a of Section 7.4 of RFC 8287.
sections.eli5: When a message says "newer kind", the checker uses the newer rules. If an old tool wrongly used the old label, the checker may just accept any kind.

sections.title: OSPFv3 in the Downstream Detailed Mapping TLV
sections.content: The protocol field of the Downstream Detailed Mapping (DDMAP) TLV in an echo reply is set to 7 when OSPFv3 is used to distribute the label carried in the Downstream Label field.
sections.eli5: In the answer message, a special number tells you the label came from the newer routing system.

sections.title: Update to RFC 8287
sections.content: RFC 8287 defined the "OSPF" code point for the Protocol field of the Segment ID sub-TLV (its Section 5) and of the DDMAP TLV (its Section 6). RFC 9214 updates it: the "OSPF" code points SHOULD be used only for OSPFv2.
sections.eli5: The old label now officially means only the old kind, so nobody mixes the two up.

sections.title: IANA Registry Changes
sections.content:
IANA assigned value 3 (OSPFv3) in the "Protocol in the Segment ID Sub-TLV" registry and value 7 (OSPFv3) in the "Protocol in Label Stack Sub-TLV of Downstream Detailed Mapping TLV" registry. Both entries reference RFC 9214.

IANA also added the note "To be used for OSPFv2 only" to the existing entry for code point 1 (OSPF) in the first registry and code point 5 (OSPF) in the second.
sections.eli5: The official list of codes got one new line for each of the two tables, plus a reminder next to the old entries.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The document updates RFC 8287 and does not introduce any additional security considerations. For the generic security considerations of MPLS LSP Ping, it points to RFC 8029.
sections.eli5: Adding a new label does not open any new doors for trouble. The older safety notes still apply.
